title: Histological characterization and quantification of newborn cells in the adult rodent brain
protocol: Transfer free-floating sections into glass scintillation vials containing the denaturing pre-treatment solution.
Wash tissue for 5 min three times (3×) with PBS at room temperature (∼20°C).
Incubate free-floating sections in 1 mL of de-ionized formamide for 2 h at 65°C.
Wash sections with 3× 5 min washes with PBS.
Incubate in 1 mL of 2 M HCl for 30 min at 37°C.
Wash sections with 2× 5 min washes with 0.1 M Borax solution.
Incubate in 1 mL of Borax solution for 20 min at room temperature.
Wash sections with 6× 5 min washes in PBS.
Dilute sheep anti-BrdU and mouse anti-NeuN antibodies in blocking solution to prepare primary antibody solutions.
Incubate free-floating sections in 1 mL of the prepared primary antibodies overnight (∼8–12 h) at room temperature.
Wash sections with 5 min washes in PBS.
Incubate tissue in 1 mL blocking solution for 30–60 min.
Incubate in secondary antibodies in blocking solution for 2 h at room temperature.
Wash three times with PBS for 5 minutes each.
Cover scintillation vials with aluminum foil during steps involving fluorophores.
Incubate with streptavidin-550 (1:400) in blocking solution for 1.5 hours at room temperature.
Wash three times for 5 minutes each in PBS.
Float tissue sections in PBS in a glass petri dish using a fine paintbrush to arrange individual sections.
Drag each section onto the coated glass slides with a fine paintbrush.
Allow slides to dry for approximately 10 minutes until sections adhere to the slide.
Apply mounting medium and place a coverslip on the slide.
Dry the mounted slides overnight (∼8–12 hours) in the dark.
Store slides at 4°C in the dark to reduce loss of signal from the fluorophore over time.
Use a Zeiss confocal microscope (LMS 780) running Zen black software (2012 SP5).
Acquire images using a 20× air objective with NA of 0.8, at a resolution of 1024×1024 and acquisition resolution of 2.4 pixels/μm.
Capture optical sections in series throughout the Z-axis for each field of view.
Use anatomical landmarks to define the striatum as the region of interest (ROI).
Utilize the tiling function to capture consecutive fields of view spanning the entire ROI.
Post-process images using the ‘stitch’ function to produce a composite 3-dimensional volume of the entire striatum.
Adjust channel-specific settings such as laser power and gain to optimize signal strength and specificity for each fluorophore.
Define the region of interest on the X and Y planes using microscope-specific software, typically defined as a ‘tiling’ feature.
Define the Z range by setting upper and lower limits at diagonally opposite points of the ROI.
Set the optical section interval according to the Nyquist principle, with an interval of 2∗pixel size (for a pixel size of 0.42 μm, set the interval at <0.84 μm).
Perform a post-processing ‘stitch’ function following image acquisition to generate a composite 3-dimensional ROI.
Handle the composite ROI as a single tissue volume in the image analysis software.
Select 'Surface’ function in the software.
Select ‘Skip automatic detection, edit manually’ for more accurate delineation of the ROI.
Select pencil tool and draw the contour of your ROI.
Use every second Z level to define the ROI on the X-Y plane to accommodate changes in depth.
Use the ‘Mask Selection’ function to apply the surface to your desired channel.
Create a duplicated channel excluding any signal outside the surface defining the ROI.
Identify and count cells within the ROI using the spot creation tool.
Select the add new Spot to begin defining parameters for automated cell detection.
Choose the option ‘Segment only a region of interest’ to preview results.
Position the sampling square in a representative portion of the image.
Create 3 sampling squares in non-uniform signal areas if necessary.
Use a single sampling square for uniformly represented markers.
Select the source channel for automated cell detection.
Define the minimum diameter of the cell population of interest as 6 μm.
Define the minimum diameter of the BrdU labeling cells as 4.5 μm.
Use background subtraction option to remove background noise.
Allocate threshold automatically according to default settings.
Verify automated cell detection using live preview feature.
Adjust spot detection threshold manually based on signal quality variability.
Set a fixed threshold for NeuN signal intensity across all brain sections.
Adjust BrdU signal threshold blindly and accordingly across different sections.
Apply the parameters selected for the sampling square to the entire ROI.
Find the number of spots/cells under the Overall tab.
Generate a new channel with the annotated representation of cells.
Repeat all steps for additional channels where required.
Invest time in image acquisition quality for efficient and accurate automated cell detection using morphometric software.
Use the spot co-localization tool for co-localization on data acquired from the spot creation sequence on >1 channel.
Run spot detection on the channels of interest.
From the ‘Tools’ tab, select the ‘Colocalize Spot Xtension’.
Select the 2 spot datasets of interest.
Define a threshold that corresponds to the distance above which the 2 spots would not be considered co-localized.
Apply a threshold of 2 μm for nuclear markers across all samples.
